scenes.text: There are more trees on Earth than stars in our galaxy.
In twenty fifteen, a team led by ecologist Thomas Crowther at Yale counted the world's trees.
They used tree measurements from hundreds of thousands of forest plots on every continent except Antarctica.
Then they added satellite images to map tree density everywhere.
Their answer, published in the journal Nature, was about three trillion trees.
Earlier estimates said only about four hundred billion.
That's roughly four hundred trees for every person alive at the time.
Now look up at the Milky Way.
Astronomers estimate it holds about one hundred to four hundred billion stars.
So Earth's trees beat our galaxy's stars by several times.
But the same study found some bad news.
Humans cut down about fifteen billion trees every year.
And since human civilization began, the number of trees has fallen by almost half.
Which surprises you more: the trees, or the stars?

title: Earth has more trees than the Milky Way has stars 🌳
caption: A 2015 Yale-led study in Nature counted about 3 trillion trees on Earth. The Milky Way has an estimated 100-400 billion stars. 🌌
